p: Worcester packs some big names into its history. King John is buried in the cathedral, right in front of the high altar, and the composer Sir Edward Elgar was born just outside the city at Lower Broadheath, where his birthplace cottage can still be visited. You'll even find a statue of Elgar near the cathedral, looking out over the city he loved.

If the Civil War story mentioned above has you curious, The Commandery is a museum in an old building that served as the Royalist headquarters during the Battle of Worcester. The Museum of Royal Worcester tells the story of the city's famous porcelain, and the Tudor House Museum on Friar Street is a charming peek into everyday life from centuries past.

Planning-wise, give yourself around an hour for a round of crazy golf, plus extra if you're bringing a big group. Turn up a few minutes early, agree on a shot limit per hole, and make sure the youngest players get a proper go rather than being hurried along. It's supposed to be fun, after all.

For a bigger day, the Malvern Hills are a short drive away and offer some of the best views in the region, while Worcester Racecourse on Pitchcroft sits right beside the river close to the centre. With all that on the doorstep, a round of golf makes a cheerful warm-up or wind-down. Cracking stuff.
